fullPassage: During World War II, there was a group of people who risked everything to protect priceless works of art from ruin. In 1943, around 345 people from 14 different Allied nations* came together to form the Monuments, Fine Arts, and Archives (MFAA) program. They were not trained soldiers but scholars and experts of various kinds, such as professors, historians, and architects. These brave men and women volunteered to protect Europe’s cultural heritage and became known as the “Monuments Men.” From Preventing Destruction to Saving Treasures When the MFAA was first formed, its main goal was to prevent the destruction of cultural landmarks. The Monuments Men persuaded the Allied forces not to bomb areas with museums, churches, or other culturally significant buildings. They also visited areas that had already been destroyed to restore damaged architecture and works of art. It wasn’t long before their role expanded. During the war, the Nazis had been stealing works of art and other cultural treasures from countries across Europe. They hid these treasures in places like castles, mines, and caves. When the Monuments Men learned about this, they started looking for the stolen treasures. Their search has since been called “the greatest treasure hunt in history.” When Germany began to lose the war, the stolen objects came under threat. Hitler ordered his forces to destroy everything that could be useful to the Allied armies before they retreated from an area. Some Nazi leaders believed that this included not just military and industrial equipment but everything of value — even the stolen works of art. A Race against the Clock at Altaussee One of the largest collections of stolen items was hidden in the salt mines of Altaussee, Austria. Upon discovering its location, some of the Monuments Men rushed to the mines. They hoped to recover everything before it was too late. Meanwhile, the Nazi leader who was in charge of the area tried to destroy everything by setting off large explosives inside the mines. This could have been disastrous. Luckily, some local miners found the explosives in the mines and came up with a plan to protect their livelihood. They secretly removed the large explosives and put smaller ones at the entrances. Once they went off, the Nazi leader believed that everything was destroyed. However, while the small explosions sealed off the entrances, they left the rest of the mines and the works of art unharmed. When the Monuments Men arrived and squeezed their way into the mines, they must have been amazed to see what was inside. There were thousands of priceless objects, including paintings, statues, books, furniture, and more. The Monuments Men thought it would take about one year to transport everything they found to a safe location. However, because control of the area was going to change at the end of the war, they would have access to the mines for just two months. With insufficient packing supplies and only a few trucks, the transporting mission seemed impossible. Not only that, but food was in short supply. Even without eating proper meals, they worked up to twenty hours a day. They used coats and gas masks as packing materials and did everything they could to accomplish this vital mission in time. In the end, the Monuments Men succeeded in rescuing thousands of stolen works of art, including important pieces such as Jan van Eyck’s Adoration of the Mystic Lamb, Johannes Vermeer’s The Astronomer, and Michelangelo’s Madonna of Bruges. The Continuing Impact of the Monuments Men The efforts of the Monuments Men did not end with the war. For several years, they continued the work of recovering cultural treasures and identifying where they had been stolen from. In the end, the Monuments Men returned more than five million works of art and objects of cultural importance to their places of origin. Not everything that was stolen by the Nazis has been found, but what the Monuments Men accomplished is truly amazing. Without this determined group, the search for stolen works of art might never have begun. In addition, countless historical and cultural landmarks would have been lost forever due to the destruction of war. It is worth remembering the Monuments Men’s contribution to the preservation of cultural heritage. Thanks to their efforts, many incredible cultural sites and works of art have survived and can still be appreciated to this day. Culture Notes Don’t Lose Your Language! Did you know that there are over 7,000 languages currently being used around the world? Most of these languages are spoken by very small groups of people, and half of them could disappear within the next generation. This would be a great loss because language plays a big role in connecting people’s identity to their culture. This is why some organizations work to preserve them. For example, a nonprofit organization called Wikitongues has set the goal of preserving all languages that are in danger of being lost. The organization works to achieve this by recording videos of individuals speaking these languages and making mother-tongue resources more accessible. Culture Notes

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② knowing → known: 'become + 과거분사'로 '~로 알려지다'
det.analysis:
❌ ① came — 'around 345 people ... came together'에서 과거의 일을 나타내는 과거형 came는 올바릅니다.

✅ ② knowing — 원래는 known입니다. 'become + 과거분사(known)'로 '~로 알려지다'라는 뜻이 되어야 해요. knowing(-ing)은 '알고 있는'이라는 능동의 뜻이라 문맥에 안 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ③ to prevent — 'its main goal was to prevent'는 'be동사 + to부정사(~하는 것)'로 목적을 나타내어 올바릅니다.

❌ ④ damaged — 'damaged architecture(손상된 건축물)'에서 명사를 꾸미는 과거분사로 올바릅니다.
det.tip: become known as ~ = ~로 알려지다 (수동/상태는 과거분사)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ including → included: that절 안에 동사가 필요 (과거형 included)
det.analysis:
❌ ① hid — 'They hid these treasures'에서 hide의 과거형 hid로 올바릅니다.

❌ ② looking — 'started looking for'는 'start + -ing(~하기 시작하다)'로 올바릅니다.

❌ ③ to destroy — 'ordered his forces to destroy'는 'order + 목적어 + to부정사'로 올바릅니다.

✅ ④ including — 원래는 included입니다. 'that this ___ not just A but B'에서 that절 안에 동사가 필요해요. 그래서 '포함했다'라는 과거형 동사 included가 맞아요. including(-ing)은 동사가 아니라 틀려요. ←정답
det.tip: this included A but B = 이것은 A뿐 아니라 B도 포함했다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① set → setting: 전치사 by 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)
det.analysis:
✅ ① set — 원래는 setting입니다. 앞의 by는 전치사인데, 전치사 뒤에는 동사를 -ing(동명사) 형태로 써야 해요. 그래서 'by setting off(~을 터뜨림으로써)'가 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ② found — 'some local miners found the explosives'에서 find의 과거형 found로 올바릅니다.

❌ ③ sealed — 'the small explosions sealed off the entrances'에서 과거형 동사 sealed로 올바릅니다.

❌ ④ amazed — 'must have been amazed(놀랐음에 틀림없다)'에서 감정을 나타내는 과거분사 amazed로 올바릅니다.
det.tip: by + -ing = ~함으로써 (전치사 뒤 동명사)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ expanded가 맞음. shrank(줄어들다)는 역할 '확대' 문맥과 반대
det.analysis:
❌ ① prevent — 'main goal was to prevent the destruction(파괴를 막는 것)'. 문화 유적을 지키는 것이 목표였으므로 적절합니다.

❌ ② restore — 'restore damaged architecture(손상된 건축물을 복원하다)'. 파괴된 곳을 되살린다는 문맥에 적절합니다.

✅ ③ shrank — 원래는 expanded입니다. 뒤 문장에서 도난 예술품까지 찾아 나서며 역할이 '확대(expanded)'되었다고 나와요. shrank(줄어들다)는 정반대라 문맥에 안 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ④ stealing — 'the Nazis had been stealing works of art(예술품을 훔치고 있었다)'. 나치의 약탈을 나타내어 적절합니다.
det.tip: role expanded = 역할이 확대되었다 (예방 → 보물 추적)

questions.passage: The Monuments Men thought it would take about one year to ①<u>transport</u> everything they found to a safe location.  However, because control of the area was going to change at the end of the war, they would have ②<u>access</u> to the mines for just two months.  With ③<u>insufficient</u> packing supplies and only a few trucks, the transporting mission seemed impossible.  Not only that, but food was in ④<u>abundant</u> supply.  Even without eating proper meals, they worked up to twenty hours a day.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ short가 맞음. abundant(풍부한)는 식량 '부족' 문맥과 반대
det.analysis:
❌ ① transport — 'one year to transport everything(모든 것을 옮기는 데 1년)'. 이송 임무 문맥에 적절합니다.

❌ ② access — 'have access to the mines(광산에 접근할 수 있다)'. 광산 출입 문맥에 적절합니다.

❌ ③ insufficient — 'insufficient packing supplies(부족한 포장 물자)'. 물자가 모자란 상황이므로 적절합니다.

✅ ④ abundant — 원래는 short입니다. 바로 앞에 'food was in short supply(식량이 부족했다)'가 있고 제대로 된 식사도 못 했다고 나와요. abundant(풍부한)는 정반대라 틀려요. ←정답
det.tip: in short supply = 공급이 부족한

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸: 첫 목표는 문화 유적의 '파괴를 막는 것(prevent the destruction)'
det.analysis:
❌ ① restore the ruins(폐허를 복원하다) — 복원은 나중에 확장된 역할이고, 첫 목표는 아니에요.

✅ ② prevent the destruction(파괴를 막다) — 빈칸 바로 뒤에서 '박물관·교회를 폭격하지 말라고 설득했다'고 하므로, 첫 목표는 문화 유적의 '파괴를 막는 것'이 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ③ record the locations(위치를 기록하다) — 본문에 없는 내용이에요.

❌ ④ sell the artworks(예술품을 팔다) — 예술품을 지키는 내용과 정반대예요.
det.tip: not to bomb ... = 폭격하지 않도록 → 파괴 방지

det.korean: 빈칸: 독일이 전쟁에 지자 도난 예술품이 '위협을 받게 되었다(came under threat)'
det.analysis:
✅ ① came under threat(위협을 받게 되었다) — 빈칸 바로 뒤에서 히틀러가 '모든 것을 파괴하라'고 명령했다고 나와요. 즉 도난 예술품이 파괴될 '위험에 처했다'는 뜻이 자연스러워요. ←정답

❌ ② were safely returned(안전하게 반환되었다) — 아직 되찾기 전이고, 오히려 파괴 위기에 놓인 상황이라 반대예요.

❌ ③ lost all their value(모든 가치를 잃었다) — 예술품의 가치가 사라졌다는 내용은 본문에 없어요.

❌ ④ were quickly forgotten(빠르게 잊혔다) — '잊혔다'가 아니라 파괴 위협을 받은 것이라 안 맞아요.
det.tip: come under threat = 위협을 받게 되다 (뒤 문장의 '파괴 명령'이 근거)

questions.passage: During World War II, there was a group of people who risked everything to protect priceless works of art from ruin.  In 1943, around 345 people from 14 different Allied nations* came together to form the Monuments, Fine Arts, and Archives (MFAA) program.  They were not trained soldiers but scholars and experts of various kinds, such as professors, historians, and architects.  These brave men and women volunteered to protect Europe’s cultural heritage and became known as the “Monuments Men. ” From Preventing Destruction to Saving Treasures When the MFAA was first formed, its main goal was to prevent the destruction of cultural landmarks.  The Monuments Men persuaded the Allied forces not to bomb areas with museums, churches, or other culturally significant buildings.  They also visited areas that had already been destroyed to restore damaged architecture and works of art.  It wasn’t long before their role expanded.  During the war, the Nazis had been stealing works of art and other cultural treasures from countries across Europe.  They hid these treasures in places like castles, mines, and caves.  When the Monuments Men learned about this, they started looking for the stolen treasures.  Their search has since been called “the greatest treasure hunt in history. ” When Germany began to lose the war, the stolen objects came under threat.  Hitler ordered his forces to destroy everything that could be useful to the Allied armies before they retreated from an area.

questions.passage: <u>A Race against the Clock</u> at Altaussee One of the largest collections of stolen items was hidden in the salt mines of Altaussee, Austria.  Upon discovering its location, some of the Monuments Men rushed to the mines.  They hoped to recover everything before it was too late.  Meanwhile, the Nazi leader who was in charge of the area tried to destroy everything by setting off large explosives inside the mines.  This could have been disastrous.  Luckily, some local miners found the explosives in the mines and came up with a plan to protect their livelihood.  They secretly removed the large explosives and put smaller ones at the entrances.  Once they went off, the Nazi leader believed that everything was destroyed.  However, while the small explosions sealed off the entrances, they left the rest of the mines and the works of art unharmed.  When the Monuments Men arrived and squeezed their way into the mines, they must have been amazed to see what was inside.  There were thousands of priceless objects, including paintings, statues, books, furniture, and more.  The Monuments Men thought it would take about one year to transport everything they found to a safe location.  However, because control of the area was going to change at the end of the war, they would have access to the mines for just two months.  With insufficient packing supplies and only a few trucks, the transporting mission seemed impossible.  Not only that, but food was in short supply.  Even without eating proper meals, they worked up to twenty hours a day.  They used coats and gas masks as packing materials and did everything they could to accomplish this vital mission in time.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 A Race against the Clock가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis: 밑줄 친 A Race against the Clock는 직역하면 '시계와의 경주'로, 시간에 쫓기는 촉박한 상황을 뜻하는 표현이에요. ❌ ① 여러 나라가 보물을 두고 벌인 경쟁 — 나라 간 경쟁이 아니라 시간과의 싸움이에요. ✅ ② 제한된 시간 안에 임무를 끝내야 하는 촉박한 상황 — 광산 접근 기간이 단 두 달뿐이고 하루 20시간씩 일했다는 내용과 맞아요. ←정답 ❌ ③ 시계를 수리하는 정교한 작업 — 실제 시계와는 관련이 없어요. ❌ ④ 밤낮으로 이어진 광부들의 노동 — 광부가 아니라 몬유먼츠 맨의 이송 임무를 가리켜요.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①은 어법상 틀렸다. 어법에 맞게 올바른 형태로 고쳐 쓰시오. (한 단어, 영어로)

det.korean: to rescue → rescuing: 전치사 in 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)를 써야 한다.
det.analysis:
밑줄이 있는 부분은 'the Monuments Men succeeded in ___ thousands of stolen works of art(몬유먼츠 맨은 수천 점의 도난 예술품을 ___ 데 성공했다)'예요.

① 핵심은 앞에 있는 in이에요. 여기서 in은 전치사인데, 전치사 뒤에는 동사를 그대로 쓰지 못하고 -ing(동명사) 형태로 바꿔야 해요.

② 그래서 '구조하다'라는 rescue는 rescuing으로 써서 'succeed in rescuing(~하는 데 성공하다)'이 돼요.

③ to rescue(to부정사)로 쓰면 전치사 in 뒤에 올 수 없어서 틀려요. 정답은 rescuing이에요.
det.tip: succeed in + -ing = ~하는 데 성공하다 (전치사 뒤 동명사)

det.analysis:
'모든 것'을 먼저 쓰고 그 뒤를 관계대명사로 꾸미는 문제예요.

① '모든 것'은 everything으로 시작해요.

② '~할 수 있는'처럼 앞의 명사를 꾸며 주는 문장은 관계대명사 that으로 이어요. 'everything that ~(~한 모든 것)'.

③ '유용할 수 있다'는 '~할 수 있다'의 could와 '~이다'의 be를 합쳐 could be useful로 써요.

④ '연합군에게'는 to the Allied armies예요. to(~에게) + the Allied armies(연합군).

전부 이으면 everything that could be useful to the Allied armies, 총 9단어예요.
det.tip: everything that + could be ~ = ~할 수 있는 모든 것 (관계대명사 that)

det.korean: 모든 것을 옮기는 데 약 1년이 걸릴 것이다.
det.analysis:
'~하는 데 (시간)이 걸리다'라는 표현을 배열하는 문제예요.

① '(시간)이 걸리다'는 'it takes + 시간'이에요. '~일 것이다'의 would를 넣어 it would take로 시작해요. 여기서 it은 특별한 뜻 없이 형식적으로 쓰는 주어예요.

② '약 1년'은 about one year예요. about이 '약, 대략'이라는 뜻이에요.

③ '모든 것을 옮기는 데'는 to transport everything이에요. to부정사가 '~하는 데'라는 뜻을 나타내요.

전부 이으면 it would take about one year to transport everything, 총 9단어예요.
